text:
What sang yesterday

No longer sings.

It died with a flower in its mouth:

In that of the thorn in its throat.


It loved water without thirst

And, certainly,

Despite having wings, it watched time

Free of need.


It was not longing or imprudence:

It was nothing.

And the day touches in silence

The misfortune caused.


If perhaps that is misfortune:

To lose one's life

Over so beautiful a rose,

For so slight a wound.

translation.title: What Sang Yesterday...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the fragile death-by-rose image and the source's uncertain judgment of misfortune.
